look_here_first: In damp compacted ground or at pond margins, look for CREEPING STOLONS (aboveground runners), and a seedhead with usually TWO slender one-sided racemes spreading from the same terminal area like a little V. A two-branch seedhead without the rooted runner could be Bahia grass or another Paspalum, so collect growth-base evidence too.

Head photographed straight on from branching joint, showing the paired racemes.
Face-on two rows of spikelets along a raceme with mm scale.
Close blade/sheath collar and a mature spikelet for P. notatum discrimination.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Knotgrass combines wet-ground creeping stolons with usually paired (rarely three) unilateral flowering racemes. Bahia grass can produce two racemes but differs in low turf/rhizome architecture and spikelet structure. Thin paspalum may form just one or a few flowering branches but has different leafy habit and varietal hair traits; Florida paspalum forms robust upright bunches and bigger oval spikelets.
